  "explanation": "The write-up only records \"g(x) > -x\" from positivity of f, which does not exclude negative values of g. Section 3 rules out two distinct positive values of V, then silently asserts V ⊆ {0} or V ⊆ {0,c}; nothing anywhere excludes g(x) < 0. This omission is load-bearing: Lemma 1 assumes b = g(z) ∈ {0,c}, and the level-set dichotomy S_0 ∪ S_c = (0,∞) in §§4–6 presumes it. Hence L5.3 (nonnegativity of the common difference) is not established as written. The standard two-line fix — g(x₀) = -d < 0 gives g(x₀ - nd) = -d with x₀ - nd > 0 for all n, impossible — is absent, so a one-sentence insertion suffices."
